draft.title: Fromelles, Pozières and the Somme
card: In 1916 Australian infantry fought on the Western Front in France. The Battle of the Somme was a huge British and French attack that began on 1 July 1916.

on 19 and 20 July, Australians attacked near the Somme to keep German troops away from the main battle. This kind of attack is called a diversion. It failed, and about 5,500 Australians became casualties in one night.
in late July and early August, Australians captured this village. They then held it under heavy German shelling and suffered many casualties.
A casualty is a soldier killed, wounded, captured or missing. In a few weeks in 1916, Australian casualties in France were higher than in the whole eight months at Gallipoli.
draft.remember: In a few weeks in France in 1916, Australia lost more men than at Gallipoli.

a.q: What do Fromelles and Pozières show about Australian losses in 1916?
opts: In weeks, losses were higher than in all of Gallipoli
Losses were lower than at Gallipoli as fights were short
Losses were higher because the fighting lasted far longer
Losses were small because Australians only guarded the line
a.why: The fighting at Fromelles and Pozières lasted only weeks, yet casualties were higher than in the eight months at Gallipoli. The option about longer fighting is tempting, but the Gallipoli campaign was the longer one.
a.clue: Compare weeks in France with eight months at Gallipoli.

b.q: Which best describes the Australian attack at Fromelles in July 1916?
opts: A diversion near the Somme with heavy losses in one night
A village captured, then shelled by German guns for weeks
A landing on a steep coast in Turkey to open a sea route
A charge by mounted troops against Ottoman defenders
b.why: Fromelles was a diversion near the Somme, and about 5,500 Australians became casualties in one night. The village held under shelling is Pozières, which is the most tempting wrong option.
b.clue: Which one was meant to draw German troops away from the main battle?

a.best: In weeks, losses were higher than in all of Gallipoli

b.best: A diversion near the Somme with heavy losses in one night

problems.detail: Fromelles was in French Flanders, about 80 km north of the Somme battlefield. It was a diversion meant to stop German troops moving south to the Somme. Saying the Australians attacked 'near the Somme' could lead students to think it was on or beside the Somme battlefield. Wording such as 'north of the Somme' or 'away from the Somme, to help the Somme battle' would be more accurate.
The right option repeats the 'diversion near the Somme' wording, which misplaces Fromelles geographically.
Australian fighting at Pozières and the ridge beyond it (to Mouquet Farm) lasted from 23 July into early September 1916, about six weeks. 'Late July and early August' understates this.

The card compares casualties (killed, wounded, captured or missing), but the remember line says 'lost more men'. Students could read that as deaths. For deaths alone the comparison with Gallipoli (about 8,700 dead) is much closer and less clear-cut, so the line should say casualties.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The card calls Fromelles 'near the Somme' when it was about 80 km north, and it understates how long the fighting at Pozières lasted. The remember line also swaps 'casualties' for 'lost more men', which students could read as deaths.

proposal.title: Fromelles, Pozières and the Somme
card: In 1916 Australian infantry fought on the Western Front in France. The Battle of the Somme was a huge British and French attack that began on 1 July 1916.

on 19 and 20 July, Australians attacked at Fromelles, about 80 km north of the Somme battlefield. The aim was to stop German troops moving south to the Somme. This kind of attack is called a diversion. It failed, and about 5,500 Australians became casualties in one night.
from 23 July to early September, Australians captured this village on the Somme and pushed along the ridge beyond it. German shelling was heavy, and casualties were very high.
A casualty is a soldier killed, wounded, captured or missing. In about seven weeks in France in 1916, Australian casualties were higher than in the whole eight months at Gallipoli.
proposal.remember: Fromelles and Pozières cost Australia more casualties in weeks than Gallipoli did in eight months.

a.clue: Compare weeks in France with eight months at Gallipoli.

b.q: Which best describes the Australian attack at Fromelles in July 1916?
opts: A diversion north of the Somme, costly in a single night
A village captured, then shelled by German guns for weeks
A landing on a steep coast in Turkey to open a sea route
A charge by mounted troops against Ottoman defenders
b.why: Fromelles was a diversion about 80 km north of the Somme battlefield, meant to stop German troops moving south. About 5,500 Australians became casualties in one night. The village held under shelling is Pozières, which is the most tempting wrong option.
